Tagcast 0.85.1 brings optional experimental gapless album playback, a dedicated Settings page and official iBroadcast service health on Overview. It also includes the album organisation and playback improvements added since 0.80.0.

## Fixed in 0.85.1 — desktop service status

The standalone app could show “Current service status unavailable” even while the official public feed was reachable. The status check now uses the HTTPS certificates already included with Tagcast, with certificate and hostname verification enabled. No settings reset is needed. Missing, failed or stale reports still remain Unknown / unavailable.

## Keep continuous albums flowing

For compatible FLAC albums, open **Settings → Playback**, choose **Original file (Premium)**, save the streaming quality, then enable **Gapless playback for albums in order**. Start a fresh run with **Play album**. Each track keeps its own time bar, with the same queue, volume, playback speed and audio output controls.

Gapless is **experimental and off by default**. It applies to normal album order; Shuffle album, Random Album, playlists and active queue synchronisation use standard playback. Preparation can take longer than ordinary streaming. Larger Original files can continue downloading beyond twenty seconds while data arrives, with bounded inactivity, total-time and memory limits.

Unsupported files, incompatible adjacent formats or decoder block sizes, and preparation or playback errors fall back to standard playback. There is no crossfade or silence trimming. Original FLAC is the primary measured path; MP3 support is separately experimental and depends on usable encoder timing information. Synthetic PCM tests establish continuity for their measured inputs, not universal sample accuracy across all music, platforms or physical outputs.

## Settings with room to work

Settings opens as a normal page inside Tagcast, organised into **Interface**, **Playback**, **Discovery**, **Sources & keys**, **Data & exports** and **About & updates**. Existing preferences, defaults and Save behaviour are preserved. Now playing and compact-player choices are under Playback, while sidebar shortcuts remain directly visible under Interface.

Development-only playback diagnostic controls have been removed from Settings. The window and player use the normal Tagcast/Gapless labels. The desktop app retains its normal profile, settings folder and stable local address.

## See official service health

Overview now includes **iBroadcast Service Status**, showing Streaming, API Server, Play Queue, Artwork and Library Generation from the official public feed. It refreshes about every five minutes while Overview is visible and shows retrieval/report times, issue details and stale or unavailable information. Public service health is clearly separate from your account connection; missing or stale data is never shown as confirmed current Operational status.

## Organise and discover albums

- Select several albums and assign an existing or new native iBroadcast tag through the existing review flow. Fully confirmed assignments deselect the reviewed albums; cancellation, errors and uncertain results retain the selection.
- Choose **Shuffle album** to start an album with a shuffled queue, alongside the existing **Play album** action.
- Browse albums in a stable random order using **Random album** in Filter and sort. The menu uses two columns where space permits and retains its narrow-window and keyboard behaviour.
- Selecting **Various Artists** makes the removal of additional album-artist credits visible in the draft, before review. Track artists remain independent.

## Downloads and upgrading

- **macOS Apple Silicon:** `tagcast-0.85.1-macos-arm64.zip`.
- **macOS Intel:** `tagcast-0.85.1-macos-x64.zip`.
- **Windows x64:** `tagcast-0.85.1-windows-x64.zip`.
- **Linux x64:** `tagcast-0.85.1-linux-x64.tar.gz`.

Each standalone download bundles the desktop app, Python server and browser CLI; no separate Python or Node.js installation is required. Every archive has a SHA-256 companion. Quit an older Tagcast before opening the new version. Existing settings, credentials, cache and local favourites remain in their normal locations. Private Gapless Test profiles are not automatically migrated.

macOS requires Ventura 13 or newer; Linux needs a graphical desktop and compatible system libraries. The apps retain ad-hoc macOS integrity signatures and are not Developer ID notarized or Windows Authenticode signed. Python/browser use remains available from the source archive. Tagcast never changes local music files.
